reply.text: `==` tests whether two objects have equal values, calling the `__eq__` method, while `is` tests whether two names refer to the exact same object in memory, comparing identities (roughly, `id(a) == id(b)`). Two lists with the same contents are `==` but not `is`, and `None` should always be checked with `is`, as in `x is None`, because it is a singleton and `is` is the idiomatic, unambiguous test. Using `is` for value comparison is a common bug: small integers and interned strings may happen to be the same object, so the code appears to work until it doesn't.
